stemBlocks.value: In trapezium ABCD, AB is parallel to DC and AD = BC. The angles at A and D are (3x + 10)° and (5x + 10)° respectively. a) Calculate the value of x. b) Calculate all four interior angles of ABCD, giving a reason for each pair of equal angles. c) State the most specific name of the trapezium.
Think first: A and D are at the two ends of the same slanted side crossing a pair of parallel lines, so they are co-interior angles.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p164-q02 from workbook page 164.

solutionSteps.instruction: Identify the angle relationship at A and D.

contentBlocks.value: AB is parallel to DC and AD is the transversal, so ∠A and ∠D are co-interior and add to 180°

solutionSteps.instruction: Use AD = BC to find the remaining angles.

contentBlocks.value: The trapezium is isosceles, so the base angles on each parallel side are equal: ∠B = ∠A and ∠C = ∠D

strategyBlocks.value: Use the co-interior pair A and D to form an equation summing to 180°, solve for x, then use AD = BC to copy the angles across to B and C.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) x = 20  (b) ∠A = 70° and ∠B = 70° (equal base angles of an isosceles trapezium); ∠D = 110° and ∠C = 110° (equal base angles on DC, each co-interior with 70°)  (c) an isosceles trapezium

whyThisWorks.value: When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, the two interior angles on the same side of it must total 180°, because together they wrap round from one parallel line to the other. The extra condition AD = BC makes the figure symmetrical about the perpendicular bisector of AB, and that mirror symmetry is what forces ∠A = ∠B and ∠D = ∠C.

commonErrors.misconception: Treating ∠A and ∠D as equal (alternate) instead of supplementary (co-interior).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Treating ∠A and ∠D as equal (alternate) instead of supplementary (co-interior).

commonErrors.misconception: Assuming ∠A and ∠C are equal, as in a parallelogram — that is false here.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Assuming ∠A and ∠C are equal, as in a parallelogram — that is false here.

commonErrors.misconception: Answering 'trapezium' for part c when the equal sides make it specifically isosceles.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Answering 'trapezium' for part c when the equal sides make it specifically isosceles.

examTip.value: Label which pair of parallel lines a transversal is crossing before deciding whether angles are equal or supplementary — the U-shape means add to 180°, the Z-shape means equal.
